title: The Grunion Run, vi
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Sixth year. Gully brings the machine's thermos. The whole beach drinks his coffee. Wood watches the town find him.

panels.composition: The beach, lanterns, the run. GULLY with a giant thermos and paper cups, a line of townspeople forming. WOOD and BARNABY at the edge, watching the line, not the fish.

characters.pose: pouring coffee for a line of people

image.prompt: a night beach festival with lanterns, a young man in a backwards cap pouring coffee from a huge thermos for a line of townspeople in rain jackets, another young man watching the line with a small dog, silver fish in the surf beyond, brush-pen black and white

balloons.text: Look at that. Six years I've been drawing this beach and he walks onto it with a thermos and it's his.

image.prompt: close-up of a young man speaking to a small dog while watching something off-panel with an unreadable expression, lantern light

panels.composition: Gully, handing a cup to an old woman. Her face. She knows him. Everyone knows him.

balloons.text: He'd have said it was too hot.

image.prompt: a young man handing a paper cup of coffee to an old woman in a rain hood who looks at him with recognition, lanterns

panels.composition: Silent. The fish. The line for coffee longer than the line for fish. Wood not drawing. Looking at Gully. The pad closed.

image.prompt: silent wide night panel of a beach where a line of people for coffee is longer than the line at the surf, a young man with a closed drawing pad watching his friend pour, small dog, silver fish, lanterns, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; xerox; black and white

notes: The town finds Gully. Wood watches it happen and closes the pad.
